items.headline: OpenAI launches Agents API in public beta
items.summary: OpenAI opened public beta access to its Agents API, exposing the same Codex harness that handles session orchestration, context compaction, and tool calling behind a single API call, letting developers build long-running autonomous agents without building their own orchestration layer.

items.headline: AI alignment pioneer Paul Christiano joins OpenAI Foundation Board
items.summary: OpenAI named Paul Christiano, founder of the Alignment Research Center and a co-inventor of RLHF, to its Foundation Board and Safety and Security Committee, adding a prominent safety researcher to its governance structure while he recuses himself from OpenAI-related matters at NIST.

items.headline: AI sales-automation startup Clay raises $115M at $7.1B valuation
items.summary: Clay, an AI-driven go-to-market platform used by Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and Stripe, closed a $115M round led by Wellington Management, more than doubling its valuation from $3.1B a year earlier as demand for AI revenue-generating agents surges.

items.headline: Oracle cloud infrastructure revenue surges 121% on AI demand
items.summary: Oracle reported Q1 FY2027 cloud infrastructure revenue of $7.4B, up 121% year-over-year, with GPU-related revenue up 177% and over 96,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GB200 units delivered, underscoring the scale of AI datacenter buildout even as GPU rental margins stay thin.

items.headline: Anthropic's Claude produces first fully verified proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
items.summary: Working largely autonomously over 11 days, Claude generated a 13-million-line, computer-checked formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem in the Lean proof assistant, proving roughly 29,500 intermediate theorems in what researchers call the largest Lean proof ever written.

items.headline: Nvidia confirms $12.93B acquisition of Hugging Face
items.summary: Nvidia finalized its purchase of Hugging Face, the platform hosting over 3 million AI models used by 18 million developers, for $12.93B, its second-largest acquisition ever, while pledging the platform will stay open to competing hardware and cloud providers.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, its first model at 'Critical' cybersecurity capability
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, calling it a generational leap in coding, science and computer use, while flagging it as the first model to cross the Critical threshold on its Preparedness Framework for cybersecurity risk, prompting added safeguards before rollout.

items.headline: Google ships Gemini 3.8 Flash and a locked-down 'Cyber' variant
items.summary: Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash, its third Flash-tier update in six weeks, built on the 3.7 Flash base but tuned for longer-horizon coding and agentic tasks, alongside a security-focused Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber variant, at unchanged pricing for now.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.3, its most capable AI model yet
items.summary: Meta rolled out Muse Spark 1.3 to developers and across Instagram, Facebook and Meta AI, narrowing the capability gap with OpenAI and Anthropic, while offering steep price discounts to users who let Meta use their prompts and outputs for future model training.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1
items.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.1, generally available with new invisible watermarking for generated text, alongside the gated Mythos 5.1 variant for cybersecurity and life-sciences use, both cutting agentic-workload costs by up to 45% via cheaper cache reads.

items.headline: Unitree completes mainland China's first humanoid robot IPO
items.summary: Unitree Robotics debuted on Shanghai's STAR Market with shares closing 460% above the IPO price after demand was oversubscribed more than 8,000 times, raising about $900M and valuing the humanoid and quadruped robot maker at roughly $9B.

items.headline: FCC bans imports of new foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots
items.summary: The U.S. FCC restricted imports of new foreign-built humanoid robots, quadrupeds and connected mobile machines on national-security grounds, targeting China's dominance of the humanoid robot market while exempting previously approved models already in the U.S.
